01.event: sent Rabbi a gift of fine linens
01.summary: A wealthy man, Bonyam ben Nunyam, sent Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi a gift of four exceptionally fine fabrics. The Gemara then describes how small each could be folded.
01.missing: Any response, consequence or change after the gift; the rest is description and word explanation.
01.reason: A single reported act cited to explain a word, with no one responding and nothing following; a bare report.

02.actor: a certain man; Rav Shimi bar Hiyya
02.event: a man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags
02.turn: Rav Shimi examined whether it was worth a peruta
02.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags, and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya, sitting before Rav, examined it to see whether it was worth a peruta. The rest is the Gemara reconciling this with Shmuel.
02.missing: Any further action or change beyond the case and its assessment; the outcome is not even stated.
02.reason: One event brought to a rabbi and a ruling, with no other narrated action or change; under R-C0's limit this is not a story.

03.missing: Any event beyond an instruction; whether it was carried out is not stated.
03.reason: Rav Nahman's arrival frames an instruction, followed by legal analysis; a setting plus a ruling is not a story.

04.event: a man came before Rabbi Yosei asking about halitza within three months
04.turn: the man pressed him why not
04.outcome: Rabbi Yosei cited a verse to justify the ruling
04.summary: A man came to Rabbi Yosei and asked whether halitza may be performed within three months. Rabbi Yosei said no; the man asked what harm it would do, and Rabbi Yosei answered with a verse.
04.missing: Any action beyond the question and answer; no change or outcome is narrated.
04.reason: Coming before a rabbi with a question and receiving an answer is the only event; question-and-answer without real conflict is not a story.

05.event: Rav Safra raised objections to Abaye's teaching
05.turn: Abaye fell silent and could not answer
05.outcome: he went to Rav Yosef, who told him the answer he should have given
05.summary: Rav Safra challenged a teaching Abaye was reciting; Abaye answered the first objection but fell silent at the second. When he came before Rav Yosef and reported it, Rav Yosef told him what he should have answered.
05.missing: Events beyond speech; the silence and the visit to Rav Yosef are the only non-verbal moments.
05.reason: Mainly scholarly dialogue, but something happens: Abaye is silenced and goes to his teacher. Sitting between borderline and not, borderline is preferred.

06.actor: Levi, Ze'eiri, Rav Shimi bar Hiyya
06.missing: Any turn or consequence; it is a list of what was brought to whom.
06.reason: A bare report of things done, cited as precedent, with nothing following.

07.actor: a yavam and yevama; Rava; Rav Sherevya
07.turn: Rava ruled halitza suffices; Rav Sherevya cited a baraita against it
07.summary: A couple who both admitted they had not consummated the levirate marriage came before Rava, who ordered halitza. Rav Sherevya objected from a baraita, and Rava accepted the objection.
07.missing: Any action besides coming before the rabbi; the ruling, challenge and retraction are speech.
07.reason: A case before a rabbi plus a ruling and standard scholarly correction; coming before him is the only event, and the challenge is ordinary Talmudic dialogue.

08.missing: Any event; it is a compliment within a legal discussion.
08.reason: Pure speech with no conflict or event.

09.missing: Any narrated event; Rav Yosef's illness is only in the translator's gloss, and the passage is Abaye reminding him of a teaching.
09.reason: Speech only, a student reminding his teacher of a teaching, with no conflict or narrated event.

10.event: a widow at her husband's grave
10.turn: (commentary: she sinned with a guard whose charge was stolen)
10.outcome: she removed her husband from the grave
10.summary: The Talmud cites the incident of a certain woman who removed her husband from his grave, as evidence that one may sin even while mourning. The surrounding details come only from the translator/commentaries.
10.missing: The incident itself; the text only alludes to it, and the plot must be filled in from commentary.
10.reason: An incident only alluded to, reconstructable only with the commentaries, is borderline under R-C6.

11.actor: a debtor, a purchaser, a creditor
11.event: a debtor owing 100 sold two plots for 50 each
11.turn: the creditor repossessed one plot and came for the other
11.outcome: the purchaser came with 100 dinars and offered the creditor a choice
11.summary: A man owing 100 dinars sold his two small plots for fifty each. His creditor seized one from the buyer and came back for the other; the buyer took 100 dinars to the creditor and told him to take the plot as worth 100 or take the money and leave both.
11.reason: A real incident with several actions and a change (sale, seizure, counter-offer), like R-C0's stolen-and-sold cow; the legal discussion follows.

12.actor: an Arab (seen by Rabba bar bar Hanna)
12.event: he cut open his camel with a sword
12.outcome: the camel died before it stopped braying
12.summary: Rabba bar bar Hanna reports seeing an Arab slash open his camel, which died so fast it had not finished braying. The Gemara uses it as an objection, which Abaye answers.
12.missing: Any protagonist response or development; it is a one-line eyewitness report cited as evidence.
12.reason: A one-line eyewitness wonder (the open case between R-C5 and a story) with two events and causality but little development; borderline is preferred over not.

13.missing: Any one-time event; these are habitual practices cited as illustration.
13.reason: Customs cited as evidence of a principle, leading nowhere; a bare report of practice.

14.event: a heretic taunted Rabban Gamliel that God had abandoned Israel
14.turn: Rabban Gamliel called him a fool and reversed the verse
14.summary: A heretic mocked Rabban Gamliel, saying God had done halitza with Israel and left them. Rabban Gamliel called him an imbecile and showed the verse says Israel removed themselves, which has no legal effect.
14.missing: Any event beyond the exchange of words.
14.reason: Speech only, but a polemical confrontation with a heretic is real conflict, so borderline under R-C2.

15.missing: Any narrated event among post-biblical figures; it is Rav Kahana's exegetical explanation of how a biblical event was carried out.
15.reason: An exegetical elaboration of a biblical episode (Jabesh-gilead), which R-S1 places out of scope; it is barely narrative at all.

16.event: his father sent him up to fetch chicks
16.turn: he fulfilled both mitzvot, sending away the mother bird
16.outcome: on the way down he fell and died
16.summary: A father told his son to climb up and bring him chicks. The son climbed, sent away the mother bird and took the young, fulfilling two mitzvot promising long life, but fell on the way back and died. Rabbi Ya'akov draws the lesson that the reward is in the World to Come.
16.reason: An actual incident (Rabbi Ya'akov saw it, per the context) with several actions and a decisive change; the exegetical conclusion is the lesson attached to it.

17.actor: Mar Yehuda; Rav Huna bar Yehuda
17.event: Mar Yehuda visited and saw people carrying among unrowed trees
17.turn: he asked whether Rav Huna rejected Avimi
17.outcome: Rav Huna answered he follows Rav Nahman
17.summary: Mar Yehuda visited Rav Huna bar Yehuda and saw people carrying among trees not planted in rows. He asked whether his host disagreed with Avimi; Rav Huna said he followed Rav Nahman.
17.missing: Any event beyond the visit framing a question and answer.
17.reason: A setting plus a question and answer, like Shabbat 147a; the visit only frames the question.

18.actor: an Amorite; a resident of Eretz Yisrael
18.event: the Amorite asked how much a Jordan palm yields
18.turn: he mocked that the Jews had ruined the land
18.outcome: the resident retorted that he meant only one side
18.summary: An Amorite asked a resident of the land how much a palm on the Jordan yielded; told sixty kor, he mocked that they had already ruined it, since his people got 120. The resident replied he was counting only one side of the tree.
18.reason: Mainly dialogue lacking actions, but with conflict (mockery and retort), so borderline under R-C2, as Jeff ruled on Ketubot 112a.

19.event: a man betrothed a minor with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace
19.outcome: Ravina ruled no concern of the father's consent
19.summary: A man betrothed a minor girl with a bundle of vegetables in the market, and Ravina ruled that a degrading betrothal raises no concern that her father approved.
19.missing: Any further action or change beyond the case and ruling.
19.reason: One event followed by a ruling, with nothing else changing; not a story under R-C0's limit.

20.missing: The incident itself; only that a case came before Rabbi Yitzhak and his ruling.
20.reason: An unnarrated case before a rabbi serves only to frame a ruling; nothing happens beyond coming before him.
